Adjusted assessment incorporating SLOOS: The FOMC statement’s positive tone on strengthening activity/employment and highly accommodative policy is broadly supported by SLOOS evidence of easing credit supply in several areas: banks eased standards on residential real estate (including GSE-eligible mortgages and HELOCs), lowered minimum credit score requirements, and eased standards on some consumer loans (credit card and auto). That said, credit conditions remain uneven: banks and foreign banks maintained tighter or unchanged standards for riskier business credit—tightening for below-investment-grade C&I while easing mainly for higher-quality borrowers—and some consumer categories remain tighter relative to pre‑pandemic levels. CRE-related lending remains cautious. Net: still moderately positive, with SLOOS suggesting incremental improvement in credit availability but with persistent caution for lower-rated borrowers and certain sectors.
